title: 好日子只會教壞功課
en: Good Times Teach Only Bad Lessons

vocab.meaning: 非常嚴重、非比尋常的事
vocab.example: I’ve been “fortunate” to have lived through some doozies
vocab.def: 美式口語，可褒可貶，指「超乎尋常」的事物。這裡指非常慘烈的市場風暴。
vocab.exzh: 我「幸運地」親身經歷過一些非常慘烈的事件

vocab.example: the Arab oil embargo, stagflation, Nifty Fifty stock collapse and “death of equities” of the 1970s
vocab.def: 政府禁止與某國或某種商品進行貿易。Arab oil embargo 指 1970 年代阿拉伯國家的石油禁運。
vocab.exzh: 1970 年代的阿拉伯石油禁運、停滯性通膨、「漂亮五十」股票崩跌與「股票已死」

vocab.example: the Arab oil embargo, stagflation, Nifty Fifty stock collapse and “death of equities” of the 1970s
vocab.def: 由 stagnation（停滯）與 inflation（通膨）合成：經濟不成長、物價卻一直漲。
vocab.exzh: 1970 年代的阿拉伯石油禁運、停滯性通膨、「漂亮五十」股票崩跌與「股票已死」

vocab.def: 金融業常用 equities 指股票，意思比 stocks 更正式，也泛指股權投資。

vocab.example: the 1994 spike in interest rates that put rate-sensitive debt instruments into freefall
vocab.def: 原指尖刺，在圖表上就是突然尖尖向上的一點。a spike in interest rates 是利率突然飆升。
vocab.exzh: 1994 年利率飆升，使對利率敏感的債務工具陷入自由落體般的暴跌

vocab.example: the 1994 spike in interest rates that put rate-sensitive debt instruments into freefall
vocab.def: 原指跳傘時還沒開傘的下墜。in freefall 比喻價格或情勢快速下跌、無法控制。
vocab.exzh: 1994 年利率飆升，使對利率敏感的債務工具陷入自由落體般的暴跌

vocab.example: the emerging market crisis, Russian default and meltdown of Long-Term Capital Management in 1998
vocab.def: 原指核反應爐熔毀，比喻機構或市場徹底崩潰。
vocab.exzh: 1998 年的新興市場危機、俄羅斯債務違約，以及長期資本管理公司的崩潰

vocab.example: the emerging market crisis, Russian default and meltdown of Long-Term Capital Management in 1998
vocab.def: 債務人還不出本金或利息。注意，在投資領域不是「預設值」的意思。
vocab.exzh: 1998 年的新興市場危機、俄羅斯債務違約，以及長期資本管理公司的崩潰

vocab.meaning: 對人格或思想形成有決定性影響的
vocab.example: Living through the 1970s was particularly formative, since so many challenges arose.
vocab.def: formative years 是「成長的關鍵年代」。課文說 1970 年代對作者的投資觀影響很深。
vocab.exzh: 親身經歷 1970 年代對我的養成特別重要，因為當時冒出了那麼多挑戰。

vocab.example: It was virtually impossible to get an investment job during the seventies
vocab.def: 表示「幾乎等於」。virtually impossible 就是「幾乎不可能」，語氣比 almost 正式。
vocab.exzh: 在七〇年代，要找到一份投資工作幾乎是不可能的

vocab.example: How many of the people who started by the sixties were still working in the late nineties when the tech bubble rolled around?
vocab.def: 指某個時間點或週期性的事件到來。the tech bubble rolled around 是說「科技泡沫那時又出現了」。
vocab.exzh: 在六〇年代就入行的人，有多少人在九〇年代後期科技泡沫出現時還在工作？

sentences.en: I like to say, “Experience is what you got when you didn’t get what you wanted.”
sentences.zh: 我常說：「經驗，就是你沒得到想要的東西時，所得到的東西。」

sentences.en: Good times teach only bad lessons: that investing is easy, that you know its secrets, and that you needn’t worry about risk.
sentences.zh: 好日子只會教壞功課：以為投資很容易、以為自己懂得其中的祕訣、以為不需要擔心風險。

sentences.en: The most valuable lessons are learned in tough times.
sentences.zh: 最有價值的教訓，是在艱困時期學到的。

sentences.en: In that sense, I’ve been “fortunate” to have lived through some doozies: the Arab oil embargo, stagflation, Nifty Fifty stock collapse and “death of equities” of the 1970s; Black Monday in 1987, when the Dow Jones Industrial Index lost 22.6 percent of its value in one day; the 1994 spike in interest rates that put rate-sensitive debt instruments into freefall; the emerging market crisis, Russian default and meltdown of Long-Term Capital Management in 1998; the bursting of the tech-stock bubble in 2000–2001; the accounting scandals of 2001–2002; and the worldwide financial crisis of 2007–2008.
sentences.zh: 就這層意義而言，我「幸運地」親身經歷過一些非常慘烈的事件：1970 年代的阿拉伯石油禁運、停滯性通膨、「漂亮五十」股票崩跌與「股票已死」；1987 年的黑色星期一，道瓊工業指數一天內蒸發了 22.6% 的價值；1994 年利率飆升，使對利率敏感的債務工具陷入自由落體般的暴跌；1998 年的新興市場危機、俄羅斯債務違約，以及長期資本管理公司的崩潰；2000 至 2001 年科技股泡沫破滅；2001 至 2002 年的會計醜聞；以及 2007 至 2008 年的全球金融危機。

sentences.en: Living through the 1970s was particularly formative, since so many challenges arose.
sentences.zh: 親身經歷 1970 年代對我的養成特別重要，因為當時冒出了那麼多挑戰。

sentences.en: It was virtually impossible to get an investment job during the seventies, meaning that in order to have experienced that decade, you had to have gotten your job before it started.
sentences.zh: 七〇年代幾乎不可能找到投資工作，也就是說，想經歷那個年代，你必須在它開始之前就已經入行。

sentences.en: How many of the people who started by the sixties were still working in the late nineties when the tech bubble rolled around?
sentences.zh: 在六〇年代就入行的人，有多少人在九〇年代後期科技泡沫出現時還在工作？

sentences.en: Most professional investors had joined the industry in the eighties or nineties and didn’t know a market decline could exceed 5 percent, the greatest drop seen between 1982 and 1999.
sentences.zh: 大多數專業投資人是在八〇或九〇年代才進入這一行，他們不知道市場跌幅可能超過 5%，因為 1982 到 1999 年間最大的跌幅就是 5%。

grammar.point: what 名詞子句當補語，雙重 get
grammar.quote: Experience is what you got when you didn’t get what you wanted.
grammar.explain:
what you got 是名詞子句，作 is 的補語，意思是「你所得到的東西」；what you wanted 也是名詞子句，作第二個 get 的受詞。
兩個 get 意思不同：got 是「得到（經驗）」，didn’t get 是「沒如願得到」。整句是個文字遊戲，意思是：沒得到想要的結果，得到的就是經驗。

grammar.point: meaning that：用分詞片語補充說明結果
grammar.quote: It was virtually impossible to get an investment job during the seventies, meaning that in order to have experienced that decade, you had to have gotten your job before it started.
grammar.explain:
meaning that … 是分詞構句，補充說明前面整句的含意，相當於 which means that…。
後面 had to have gotten 是「必須是已經取得」：had to ＋ have ＋ 過去分詞，表示在那個時間點之前，事情必須已經完成。
